# Migration: v2.7 → v2.8

## Summary

v2.7 shipped the frontmatter layer with a **single-file lint**: `docs/lint.ts`,
driven by `bun docs/lint.ts`, `--json` and `--report`. v2.8 replaces that file
with the **`pdocs` CLI** under `scripts/pdocs/` — the same rules, reorganised
into a command surface (`check`, `report`, `graph`, `find`, `backlinks`,
`orphans`, `new`) with a shared output envelope and a document registry that
both the checker and the writer read.

`docs/lint.ts` is **deleted**, not deprecated. Nothing in the scaffold ships it
any more and nothing calls it.

**Does this migration apply to you?** It applies if `docs/lint.ts` exists:

```bash
[ -f docs/lint.ts ] && echo "run this migration" || echo "already on the CLI — skip this migration"
```

That file is the whole population this migration is for: it exists only in a
project that installed the v2.7 layer in its original single-file form, and
nothing since has written it. Deleting it is step 5, so the check is also what
tells you the migration is done.

Check that rather than the `docs_version` number, which says which scaffold
release you last copied from and not which structural migrations you have
applied — see [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#how-versioning-works). The `vX-to-vY` names
are labels in their own structural sequence.

**If you are coming from v2.6, you will not need this guide.**
[v2.6-to-v2.7.md](./v2.6-to-v2.7.md) generates from the **live** template, so
today it installs `scripts/pdocs/` directly and never creates `docs/lint.ts` — a
v2.6 project lands on current tooling in one hop, and the check above sends it
straight past this file. This guide exists for a project that ran that guide
**before** it was fixed, and is sitting on the single-file lint. Running it
anyway is harmless: every step below is a copy, a delete of a file that is
already gone, or an edit that is already made.

**Docs root.** Every path below is written as `docs/`. If your
`.project-docs.json` names a different `docsRoot`, substitute it throughout —
including in the applicability test above and the whole Verification section.
`scripts/pdocs/` is **not** under the docs root and does not move with it.

## What's New

| Path                             | What it is                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scripts/pdocs/cli.ts`           | The entry point. `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts <command>`, with `--help`, `--version` and a `--format text\|json` on every command. |
| `scripts/pdocs/commands/`        | One file per command: `check`, `report`, `graph`, `find`, `backlinks`, `orphans`, `new`.                                        |
| `scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts`    | The rules that were `docs/lint.ts`, unchanged in what they enforce.                                                             |
| `scripts/pdocs/lint/registry.ts` | The document registry — folder, filename, template and lifecycle vocabulary per type. The checker and `new` both read it.       |
| `scripts/pdocs/envelope.ts`      | The shared output envelope and exit-code bands.                                                                                 |
| `scripts/pdocs/pages.ts`         | The page model `graph`, `find` and `backlinks` are built on.                                                                    |

`scripts/pdocs/` is **delivered, not handed over.** It ships production files
only — no tests, no `tsconfig.json`, no `package.json`. It is versioned with the
scaffold and this skill replaces it wholesale; nothing in it is yours to edit,
typecheck or test. If you migrated an earlier v2.8 build that did ship those,
step 6 removes them.

**The command you type changes.** Every invocation in your documents, hooks and
CI needs re-pointing; step 9 does it.

| v2.7                        | v2.8                                           |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `bun docs/lint.ts`          | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check`               |
| `bun docs/lint.ts --report` | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts report`              |
| `bun docs/lint.ts --json`   | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts graph --format json` |
| _(no equivalent)_           | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts orphans`             |
| _(no equivalent)_           | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts new <type> <name>`   |

**The CLI is the interface, and nothing wraps it.** The scaffold ships no
`package.json`, so there are no `docs:*` shorthands to keep in step with the
CLI's own surface — invoke it directly, and run `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts help`
to find the rest of it. You may still add your own shortcuts; if you do, **pin
`--format`**, because `pdocs` prints text on a terminal and JSON everywhere
else, and `npm run` inherits a TTY. That a shorthand has to defeat the CLI's own
format resolution to be useful is most of the reason the scaffold stopped
shipping one.

## What Moved

| From                                                 | To                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `docs/lint.ts`                                       | `scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts`                    |
| `scripts/docs-lint/{index,config,unlinted-links}.ts` | `scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/`, **changed** (step 4) |

**The portable core moved inside the CLI.** It used to land beside `pdocs/` as a
second directory in your `scripts/` folder, which is yours and not ours — the
split between the core and the rules that drive it is an implementation detail
of this tool, and it does not belong in your tree as something to account for.
`scripts/pdocs/` is now the one directory you are delivered, and step 4 deletes
the old location.

It is also **not unchanged, and step 4 is not optional.** `index.ts` gained two
exported interfaces (`DocsLintNode`, `DocsLintReport`) and its walk was split in
two: `collectDocsLint` computes the report and prints nothing, and `runDocsLint`
is the printing wrapper over it. `scripts/pdocs/` imports `collectDocsLint`,
because a CLI that owns its own output envelope cannot use a function that can
only print — **on a stale portable core, the CLI fails to import on its first
run.** `walkMarkdown` also sorts its entries now, so the lint's output order no
longer depends on `readdirSync`. The comments that named `docs/lint.ts` as the
home of project-specific behaviour were updated to name
`scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts` in the same pass. The refresh also brings
`index.test.ts`, which the scaffold ships and the v2.6 → v2.7 guide never
copied.

## What's Removed

- **`docs/lint.ts`** — deleted in step 5.
- **`docs/lint.test.ts`**, if your project wrote one — deleted in the same step;
  the CLI's own tests live beside it under `scripts/pdocs/`.
- **The `--json` and `--report` flags.** They are commands now, not flags.

Nothing under `docs/` changes shape and no document moves. One document type is
**added**: `DEV_KICKOFF.md` used to be typed `handoff`, and is now its own
`kickoff` type — which leaves `handoff` for `projects/*/handoff.md`. That is a
change to your `docs/SCHEMA.md`, and step 7 makes it. **The lint fails until you
do.**

## Step-by-Step Migration

### [Agent] 1. Commit or stash your work first

Steps 4, 8 and 9 write across `docs/` and `scripts/` in bulk. Start clean so the
diff is reviewable.

```bash
git status --short
```

Anything listed: commit it or stash it before continuing.

### [Agent] 2. Install Bun and cookiecutter

```bash
command -v bun || curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
command -v cookiecutter || pipx install cookiecutter
bun --version && cookiecutter --version
```

### [Agent] 3. Generate the current scaffold locally

Two flags matter. `--no-input` is required or cookiecutter prompts and hangs
with no terminal. And `install_target="New project folder"` is required
**because `--no-input` picks the first choice**, which is the current-directory
install — that branch moves the payload's pieces out and deletes the rest,
leaving you without the reference copy this migration reads from.

```bash
rm -rf .scaffold-tmp
cookiecutter gh:ichabodcole/project-docs-scaffold-template --no-input \
  -o .scaffold-tmp install_target="New project folder"
SCAFFOLD=$(ls -d .scaffold-tmp/*/ | head -1)
echo "scaffold at: $SCAFFOLD"
```

Verify — this is the **project root**, not its `docs/`:

```bash
ls "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs/cli.ts" "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/index.ts"
```

**`$SCAFFOLD` does not survive between commands.** Steps 4, 8 and 12 all use it,
and an agent running each block as a separate shell gets an empty variable — at
which point `cp -R "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs/."` copies from `/scripts/pdocs/`
and step 12 writes `docs_version: ""`, both **exiting 0**. Either re-run the
`SCAFFOLD=$(...)` line at the top of every later block, or read the path off the
`echo` above once and paste the literal path into steps 4, 8 and 12. Confirm it
is set before each of those steps:

```bash
[ -n "$SCAFFOLD" ] && [ -d "$SCAFFOLD" ] && echo "SCAFFOLD ok: $SCAFFOLD" \
  || echo "STOP — re-derive SCAFFOLD"
```

### [Agent] 4. Copy the CLI in, and refresh the portable core

```bash
# `/.` copies the CONTENTS of the directory, so re-running this refreshes the
# tree instead of nesting a second `pdocs/` inside it. The portable core comes
# with it — it lives at scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/ now.
mkdir -p scripts/pdocs
cp -R "$SCAFFOLD/scripts/pdocs/." scripts/pdocs/

# The old location. Leaving it behind leaves a second, now-unreferenced copy of
# the core in your tree, and `git grep` will keep finding it.
rm -rf scripts/docs-lint
```

**This is an overwrite, not a merge.** `scripts/pdocs/` is delivered whole and
is supposed to match its source byte for byte — if you edited anything in it,
you edited the wrong file; the seam for project-specific rules is `extraChecks`,
and step 5 says where it lives now.

Verify:

```bash
ls scripts/pdocs/cli.ts scripts/pdocs/commands/ scripts/pdocs/lint/
ls scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/index.ts scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/config.ts \
   scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/unlinted-links.ts
ls scripts/docs-lint 2>/dev/null && echo "FAIL — the old core is still there" \
  || echo "old location gone"
```

### [Agent] 5. Delete `docs/lint.ts`

**First, check whether it is still the file the scaffold shipped.** It was the
seam for project-specific rules, so if you added any, they are in this file and
nowhere else:

```bash
git log --oneline -- docs/lint.ts
```

One commit — the one that installed it during v2.6 → v2.7 — means nothing of
yours is in it. More than one means you edited it: read
`git diff <that-first-sha>..HEAD -- docs/lint.ts` and port what you added into
`scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts`, which is the same `extraChecks` seam at its new
address. Do that before deleting, not after.

```bash
rm -f docs/lint.ts docs/lint.test.ts
```

Verify — expect no output from either:

```bash
ls docs/lint.ts docs/lint.test.ts 2>/dev/null
ls docs/*.ts 2>/dev/null
```

A `.ts` file still listed by the second command is one of yours. It keeps
working — your `tsconfig.json` is yours and step 6 only takes `scripts/` back
out of it — but it can no longer import from `docs/lint.ts`.

### [Agent] 6. Remove the development artefacts an earlier build installed

Earlier scaffolds shipped the CLI's own test suite, a `tsconfig.json` and a
`package.json` wrapping the CLI in `docs:*` scripts. None of that is yours, and
two of the three actively cost you something.

**Delete the shipped tests.** They test the CLI, they are not in the payload any
more, and `bun test` in your project runs them:

```bash
rm -f scripts/pdocs/cli.test.ts scripts/pdocs/test-env.ts \
      scripts/pdocs/commands/new.test.ts scripts/pdocs/commands/read.test.ts \
      scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.test.ts scripts/pdocs/lint/registry.test.ts \
      scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/index.test.ts
```

**Take
`scripts/**/\*.ts`back out of your`tsconfig.json` `include`,** if a previous migration put it there. The CLI imports with explicit `.ts`specifiers and assumes`types:
["bun"]`; under a conventional `tsconfig`its production files alone raise **74 errors** — 29 of them`TS5097`,
"an import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when
'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled". Typechecking delivered code you do not
own buys nothing and can fail your build:

```json
{
  "include": ["docs/**/*.ts"]
}
```

If `docs/**/*.ts` now matches nothing, `tsc` fails the whole run with
`error TS18003: No inputs were found in config file`. Drop the entry, or point
`include` at your own sources.

**The `docs:*` scripts are yours to keep or drop.** They still work — they name
the CLI — but the scaffold no longer ships or expects them, and this guide
invokes the CLI directly everywhere below. If you keep them, keep the `--format`
pin on each.

Verify:

```bash
ls scripts/pdocs/*.test.ts 2>/dev/null | wc -l   # expect 0
grep -c 'scripts/\*\*/\*\.ts' tsconfig.json 2>/dev/null   # expect 0
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text
```

### [Agent] 7. Add the `kickoff` row to `docs/SCHEMA.md`

**Do this before step 8.** Every verification from here on ends in
`docs-lint: clean`, and not one of them can while this row is missing.

`DEV_KICKOFF.md` used to be typed `handoff`; v2.8 gives it its own `kickoff`
type and leaves `handoff` for `projects/*/handoff.md`. The lint proves
SCHEMA.md's "Lifecycle by type" table equal to the registry it enforces, so a
table that has not grown the row fails the gate:

```
SCHEMA MISSING TYPE  SCHEMA.md: the lint enforces `kickoff`, the table omits it
```

Find the row:

```bash
grep -n 'handoff' docs/SCHEMA.md
```

Replace that one row:

```
| `handoff`           | —                                                                              | thin  | `projects/*/DEV_KICKOFF.md`       |
```

with these two:

```
| `kickoff` | — | thin | `projects/*/DEV_KICKOFF.md` |
| `handoff` | — | thin | `projects/*/handoff.md` |
```

Column padding does not matter — step 10 runs Prettier, which realigns the
table. **The order does:** the table is read against the registry's own order,
and `kickoff` comes before `handoff` there.

**The path column matters and the lint cannot check it.** `schemaTableChecks`
compares type against vocabulary and nothing else, so a `handoff` row still
pointing at `projects/*/DEV_KICKOFF.md` passes the gate while telling every
future reader the wrong thing. That half of this step you have to get right by
reading.

Then the paragraph below the table, which still explains the old single type:

```
for. A `handoff` is the same: a kickoff briefing, written once and read at the
start.
```

becomes:

```
for. A `kickoff` is the same: a briefing written once and read at the start of
implementation. A `handoff` is its bookend — what shipping the work requires
once it is built, written at finalization and read at deploy.
```

Verify — the row is there, the paths are right, and the gate agrees:

```bash
grep -n 'kickoff\|handoff' docs/SCHEMA.md
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text
```

Expect a `kickoff` row naming `DEV_KICKOFF.md`, a `handoff` row naming
`handoff.md`, and `docs-lint: clean`. If you already keep a
`docs/projects/*/handoff.md` of your own, it stays typed `handoff`; nothing
about the file changes, and both types carry no lifecycle either way.

### [Agent] 8. Refresh the templates, and `docs/AGENTS.md`

Not cosmetic. The templates' example links were bare Markdown links to files
that do not exist (`[Related architecture doc](./other-doc.md)`), and
`pdocs new` copies a template's body into the document it creates — so every
page created from a stale template arrives with broken links and fails the gate
immediately. The current templates fence those examples in backticks. Refreshing
them is what makes `pdocs new` usable.

This copies every template the scaffold ships, into every folder your project
already has. A folder you deliberately dropped stays dropped:

```bash
while IFS= read -r t; do
  if [ -d "docs/$(dirname "$t")" ]; then
    cp "$SCAFFOLD/docs/$t" "docs/$t" && echo "refreshed $t"
  fi
done < <(cd "$SCAFFOLD/docs" && find . -type f -name '*.md' | grep -i template | sed 's|^\./||' | sort)
```

Expect 19 `refreshed` lines on a project that kept every document type.

**Overwrite, unless you customized a template.** If you did, diff it first
(`diff "docs/$t" "$SCAFFOLD/docs/$t"`) and merge by hand: take the backticked
example links, keep your body.

Verify — this creates one page from a template, checks it, and removes it. It is
the only verification that actually exercises the reason for this step:

```bash
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts new architecture migration-probe --format text
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text
git checkout -- docs/index.md && rm -f docs/architecture/migration-probe-architecture.md
```

Expect `docs-lint: clean`. `MISSING FILE` lines naming `migration-probe` mean a
template did not get refreshed.

**Then `docs/AGENTS.md`, for the same reason.** It is what an agent reads on
entering the docs tree, and the v2.7 copy describes folders and lifecycle only —
it has no idea a CLI exists, so an agent that reads it writes documents by hand
and fails the gate on frontmatter it was never told about. The scaffold's copy
now carries a `## Creating and Querying Documents` section.

Settle whether the file is still the one the scaffold shipped, the same way step
5 settles it for `docs/lint.ts` — a `diff` alone cannot tell "the scaffold moved
on" from "we edited this":

```bash
git log --oneline -- docs/AGENTS.md
diff docs/AGENTS.md "$SCAFFOLD/docs/AGENTS.md"
```

One commit in the log — the one that installed it — means nothing of yours is in
the file, whatever the diff shows. Overwrite:

```bash
cp "$SCAFFOLD/docs/AGENTS.md" docs/AGENTS.md
```

More than one commit means you edited it: keep your version and paste the
`## Creating and Querying Documents` section in by hand. Verify either way:

```bash
grep -n 'pdocs' docs/AGENTS.md
```

Root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` is the other half of this and is **not** a file
this migration touches — it is project-specific and nothing mirrors it. Step 9
re-points its stale commands; the section that says the CLI creates documents is
[the Documentation CLI pointer](../SKILL.md#documentation-cli-pointer), which
`update-project-docs` Step 6 recommends after this guide finishes.

### [Agent] 9. Re-point every remaining reference to `docs/lint.ts`

The command names in your own prose, your pre-commit hook and your CI workflow
all still point at a file you deleted in step 5. A hook that does breaks every
commit.

Find them — `git grep` covers tracked files of every kind, which is the point
here; the references are not only in Markdown:

```bash
git grep -ln 'docs/lint\.ts' -- ':!scripts/pdocs'
```

**The two exclusions are required, not tidiness.** The CLI you copied in at step
4 cites `docs/lint.ts` by name in its own comments, on purpose — four files
record that their output is a byte-for-byte inheritance from what that file
printed, which is the reason the migration is invisible to anyone reading the
lint's output. Rewriting those comments to name the file they live in makes the
record say nothing. They are untracked the first time you run this, so an
unscoped `git grep` misses them and looks fine; commit between steps 4 and 9 —
or re-run this guide on a migrated tree — and it silently edits four source
files.

Then rewrite, longest pattern first so `--report` and `--json` are consumed
before the bare form:

```bash
git grep -ln 'docs/lint\.ts' -- ':!scripts/pdocs' \
| while IFS= read -r f; do
  sed -i.bak \
    -e 's|bun docs/lint\.ts --report|bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts report|g' \
    -e 's|bun docs/lint\.ts --json|bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts graph --format json|g' \
    -e 's|bun docs/lint\.ts|bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check|g' \
    -e 's|docs/lint\.ts|scripts/pdocs/cli.ts|g' "$f" && rm "$f.bak"
done
```

In a project that has kept the scaffold's own pages this lands in
`docs/SCHEMA.md`, `docs/README.md` and `docs/cycles/README.md`, plus anything of
yours.

**Then read the rewritten lines.** The replacement is longer than what it
replaced, so a fenced block whose comments were column-aligned comes out ragged
and Prettier will not fix it — nothing reformats inside a fence.
`docs/SCHEMA.md` has one such block under `## Running the lint`; re-space it by
hand:

```bash
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check                # the gate
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts report               # what is missing — the backfill worklist
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts graph --format json  # the whole graph as JSON
```

Verify — expect no output:

```bash
git grep -n 'docs/lint\.ts' -- ':!scripts/pdocs'
```

### [Agent] 10. Run the formatter

Step 9 changed line lengths in prose.

```bash
npx prettier --write "docs/**/*.md"    # skip if the project has no Prettier
```

### [Agent] 11. Verify the tree against the CLI

```bash
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text
bun test   # your own suite, if the project has one
```

Expect `docs-lint: clean`, and a suite that runs only your own tests — the CLI's
are not installed, and step 6 removed them if an earlier build put them there.

### [Agent] 12. Update the version markers and clean up

Both markers carry the same value: the scaffold release you migrated from.

```bash
VERSION=$(grep -m1 docs_version "$SCAFFOLD/docs/README.md" | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
echo "migrating to $VERSION"

sed -i.bak -E "s/^docs_version: \".*\"/docs_version: \"$VERSION\"/" docs/README.md && rm docs/README.md.bak
sed -i.bak -E "s/(\"version\": )\"[^\"]*\"/\1\"$VERSION\"/" .project-docs.json && rm .project-docs.json.bak
```

Confirm they agree, then remove the scaffold:

```bash
grep docs_version docs/README.md
grep '"version"' .project-docs.json
rm -rf .scaffold-tmp
```

## Cross-Reference Updates

**No path changes under `docs/`**, so no document link needs rewriting. The one
class of reference that does change is the **command**, and step 9 rewrites all
of it:

| Broken after step 5         | Fixed                                          |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `bun docs/lint.ts`          | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check`               |
| `bun docs/lint.ts --report` | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts report`              |
| `bun docs/lint.ts --json`   | `bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts graph --format json` |
| `docs/lint.ts` (bare)       | `scripts/pdocs/cli.ts`                         |

Three places outside `docs/` are worth naming, because a grep scoped to
`docs/**/*.md` misses all of them and two of them are load-bearing:

- `.husky/pre-commit`
- `.github/workflows/*.yml`
- root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`

And one place that must **not** be rewritten, which is why step 9 excludes it:
`scripts/pdocs/` names `docs/lint.ts` in its own comments deliberately, as the
thing their output is inherited from.

## Verification

```bash
# The CLI is installed and the single-file lint is gone
ls scripts/pdocs/cli.ts scripts/pdocs/commands/ scripts/pdocs/lint/
ls docs/lint.ts 2>/dev/null && echo "FAIL — still present" || echo "lint.ts removed"

# The portable core is intact
ls scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/index.ts scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/config.ts \
   scripts/pdocs/docs-lint/unlinted-links.ts
ls scripts/docs-lint 2>/dev/null && echo "FAIL — old core location" || echo "one directory"

# No development artefacts were left behind
ls scripts/pdocs/*.test.ts scripts/pdocs/test-env.ts 2>/dev/null \
  && echo "FAIL — the CLI's tests are still installed" || echo "no shipped tests"
grep -q 'scripts/\*\*/\*\.ts' tsconfig.json 2>/dev/null \
  && echo "FAIL — tsconfig still typechecks delivered code" || echo "tsconfig is yours"

# Nothing anywhere still names the deleted file
git grep -n 'docs/lint\.ts' -- ':!scripts/pdocs' \
  && echo "FAIL — stale references" || echo "no stale references"

# SCHEMA.md's table carries the new type, and points at the right files
grep -q '`kickoff`' docs/SCHEMA.md && echo "kickoff row present" \
  || echo "FAIL — step 7 not applied"
grep -q 'projects/\*/handoff.md' docs/SCHEMA.md && echo "handoff row re-pointed"

# The gate is green
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text

# The docs tree's own entry point names the CLI
grep -q 'pdocs' docs/AGENTS.md && echo "docs/AGENTS.md refreshed" \
  || echo "FAIL — step 8 not applied"

# A document created from a refreshed template passes the gate
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts new architecture migration-probe --format text
bun scripts/pdocs/cli.ts check --format text
git checkout -- docs/index.md && rm -f docs/architecture/migration-probe-architecture.md

# The two version markers agree
grep docs_version docs/README.md
grep '"version"' .project-docs.json

# Scaffold cleanup
[ ! -d .scaffold-tmp ] && echo "cleaned"
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Committed or stashed work so the tree was clean
- [ ] Installed Bun and cookiecutter
- [ ] Generated the scaffold with `--no-input` and resolved `$SCAFFOLD`
- [ ] Copied `scripts/pdocs/` and removed the old `scripts/docs-lint/`
- [ ] Checked `git log -- docs/lint.ts` for edits of your own, and ported any
      into `scripts/pdocs/lint/rules.ts`
- [ ] Deleted `docs/lint.ts` and `docs/lint.test.ts`
- [ ] Deleted the CLI's tests, took `scripts/**/*.ts` back out of
      `tsconfig.json`, and decided whether to keep any `docs:*` shortcuts
- [ ] Added the `kickoff` row to `docs/SCHEMA.md`'s "Lifecycle by type" table,
      re-pointed the `handoff` row at `projects/*/handoff.md`, and rewrote the
      paragraph below the table
- [ ] Refreshed every template, and created one document from one to prove it
- [ ] Refreshed `docs/AGENTS.md` so the docs tree's own entry point names the
      CLI
- [ ] Re-pointed every `docs/lint.ts` reference, including `.husky/pre-commit`,
      `.github/workflows/` and root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` — and left the CLI's
      own historical comments under `scripts/` alone
- [ ] Re-spaced the aligned code block in `docs/SCHEMA.md`
